_comment: Path -> the skills that must be loaded before writing that path. EVERY matching row fires, not the
first: the area floors and layer routes always apply, and a specific row below ADDS to them.
The convention this table follows — the layered floor+route model, why a row keyed on a top-level
directory cannot port to a carved repo while one keyed on architecture ports verbatim, and the
field semantics — is the `skill-routes` skill in Concertable/agent-standards.
This file is emitted by that convention's generator (.agents/gen_skill_routes.py);
Every skill is plugin-qualified so a global catalogue cannot resolve a route through an older or
a carved repo derives its table rather than hand-copying one, so re-run the generator, do not edit

routes.note: The lifecycle and method a plan or ledger must satisfy - what each artifact is, its phases and their gates, when a useful context continues versus transfers, when the artifact is deleted, the two dependency graphs, cross-plan blockers. This repo's layout, hooks and commands are plans/AGENTS.md; the exact prompt for a selected context transfer is the handoff skill.
Debt is recorded in the TECH_DEBT.md of the area that owns the problem, and the whole entry is deleted once fixed - never kept as an archive.
Writing guidance is the moment one-rule-one-home is won or lost: check docs/INDEX.md for an existing owner first, and never add a second copy of a rule that already has one.
The review-file lifecycle used to arrive from a reviews/AGENTS.md sitting in the directory. That doc is now the shared standard, so this row is what delivers it.
Area floor. Every C# file gets the style and naming standard, so a shape nobody wrote a route for is still gated. Specific routes below add to this, they do not replace it.
Layer route. Keyed on the layer the project name declares rather than on a filename suffix, because a suffix rule only covers the names someone thought to enumerate.

deny.reason: This is a *.UnitTests project and this code boots a host, container or database. That makes it an integration test. Put it in this service's *.IntegrationTests project, which owns the fixture that boots the real Program. The build enforces this too (api/TestConventions.targets).

routes.note: The architecture tier holds both static ArchUnitNET rules (module-structure) and dynamic host-graph checks (composition-testing). The host-graph checks build each host's real production registration graph without starting it, then ValidateComposition proves the roots ValidateOnBuild cannot. Every executable host is covered here or declares a CompositionValidationExclusion.
Creating a test project is the classification moment: decide unit vs integration BEFORE the name exists, because the name is what declares the tier and the build fails a name that states none.
A context IS a tenancy stance - which base it derives from decides what every query through it can see. Only B2B has tenanted stances; the per-module roster is api/Concertable.B2B/CODE_PATTERNS.md.
Mapping a table another module owns needs ExcludeFromMigrations here, or two migrations claim the same table.
A state change announces itself by raising on the entity; the pre-commit handler is what turns that into a published integration event, so the outbox row commits with the write.

The rule whose violation is silent and expensive: a seeder may only write what production code writes directly. If the only production write is a handler reacting to an event, drive the event. The forbidden-table roster is the seeding skill.
A data service WaitFor-ing another data service is the bug to never introduce. The live topology is the microservice-boundaries skill.

The universal shared tier every service consumes. Shared code is the intersection of what its consumers need, never the union - an audience-specific member bolted onto a Kernel or Contracts type is the silent, expensive violation.

Build and package config is per service folder by design - there is deliberately no repo-root version or build config, because a carve takes only the service folder and would leave anything above it behind.

Shared build infra sitting above the service folders. Allowed there only because every import of it is Exists()-guarded, so a carve that leaves the file behind degrades to the intended package-only shape instead of failing to restore. Keyed on the file name, not on api/, so the row ports verbatim into a carved repo where the same file sits at the root.
